subject: group.equal="thresholds" (categorical data measurement invariance) appears to not be acting properly

messages.author: 6954b532434a56ef
messages.subject: group.equal="thresholds" (categorical data measurement invariance) appears to not be acting properly
parts:
Degrees of freedom (df) go down from weak to strong invariance using syntax as follows:

weak<- cfa(labcost, data = WERS2,group = "thr",group.equal = "loadings",ordered=c("tcircles","tsuggest","tbrief","tindpbr","tcolpbr","ttrncom","ttrnteam"))

strong<- cfa(labcost, data = WERS2, group = 'thr', group.equal = c('loadings','thresholds'),ordered=c("tcircles","tsuggest","tbrief","tindpbr","tcolpbr","ttrncom","ttrnteam"))

When manually constraining variables the thresholds, the df acts properly (i.e. goes up).  Any thoughts here?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: group.equal="thresholds" (categorical data measurement invariance) appears to not be acting properly
parts:
It helps to have a reproducible example, so I used some data from an Mplus example available online:

myData <- read.table("http://www.statmodel.com/usersguide/chap5/ex5.16.dat")
names(myData) <- c("u1","u2","u3","u4","u5","u6","x1","x2","x3","g")
myData$u1 <- ordered(myData$u1)
myData$u2 <- ordered(myData$u2)
myData$u3 <- ordered(myData$u3)
myData$u4 <- ordered(myData$u4)
myData$u5 <- ordered(myData$u5)
myData$u6 <- ordered(myData$u6)

model <- '
f1 =~ u1 + u2 + u3
f2 =~ u4 + u5 + u6
'

fit0 <- cfa(model, data = myData, ordered = paste0("u", 1:6),
            group = "g", group.equal = c("loadings","thresholds"))
fit1 <- cfa(model, data = myData, ordered = paste0("u", 1:6),
            group = "g", group.equal = "loadings")

The parameter table shows why the degrees of freedom decrease.  

partable(fit0)
partable(fit1)


When you constrain only the loadings, the scale parameters (partable(fit0)$op == "~*~") are fixed to 1 in both groups.  When you also constrain the thresholds to equality, the scale parameters are only fixed to 1 in the first group, and estimated for group 2 (in this example).

I am not familiar enough with parameterization and constraints for categorical CFA to know whether this is what is supposed to happen, but I would guess that is what happened with your data, too.

Terry

messages.subject: Re: group.equal="thresholds" (categorical data measurement invariance) appears to not be acting properly
parts:
I have three things here:

1. Df from Terry's example is going down. 
2. You should use theta parameterization to run multiple-group categorical CFA. You will deal with item residual variance rather than item scaling parameter. 
3. You should write the script for each step manually. Otherwise, you might not test the model you wanted. For example, you need the factor mean in Group 2 to be free in the strong model but this script did not do it automatically.

You could see my website for examples.

http://www.myweb.ttu.edu/spornpra/catInvariance.html

Just for reference, this is what Mplus is doing too. See:

http://www.statmodel.com/examples/webnote.shtml#web4

That does not mean this the only (or best) approach. The Millsap and
Yun-Tein (2004) approach is nicely described here:

http://www.myweb.ttu.edu/spornpra/catInvariance.html

Yves.

messages.author: d64c3f04f3604825
messages.subject: Re: group.equal="thresholds" (categorical data measurement invariance) appears to not be acting properly
parts:
On 04/22/2015 10:07 PM, Terrence Jorgensen wrote:
> When you constrain only the loadings, the scale parameters
> (partable(fit0)$op == "~*~") are fixed to 1 in both groups.  When you
> also constrain the thresholds to equality, the scale parameters are only
> fixed to 1 in the first group, and estimated for group 2 (in this example).

So doesn't this mean that the scalar invariance model is not nested within the metric invariant model? 

If I am thinking about this correctly, the metric invariance model constrains the loading and scale parameters but the scalar invariance model constrains the loadings and thresholds but now frees the scaling in the second group.

Thanks for your thoughts on this!
John

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: group.equal="thresholds" (categorical data measurement invariance) appears to not be acting properly
parts:
So doesn't this mean that the scalar invariance model is not nested within the metric invariant model? 

If I am thinking about this correctly, the metric invariance model constrains the loading and scale parameters but the scalar invariance model constrains the loadings and thresholds but now frees the scaling in the second group.

The idea of parameter nesting gets very tricky when thresholds are part of the model, because thresholds are related to both the location and scale of the variables (mean and covariance structure of the model), as opposed to means and covariance structure being independent of entities with MV-normal data.  Millsap & Yun-Tien (2004) provide an excellent discussion of how to test measurement invariance using minimal constraints:

http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1207/S15327906MBR3903_4

Although I forget how clearly they describe the nesting of models, I know they show that you cannot discriminate between metric and scalar invariance with only binary items.  If thresholds differ across groups/time, it could be because the mean of the latent response differs, or the variance differs (or both), but there is not enough information to distinguish which.  So differences in factor loadings will not be able to show poor fit because that misspecification can just be re-expressed as a difference in thresholds.  Not sure if this is your situation, but it's just an example of how thresholds make things less intuitive, so parameter-counting heuristics might not apply like the do to continuous data.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: d64c3f04f3604825
messages.subject: Re: group.equal="thresholds" (categorical data measurement invariance) appears to not be acting properly
parts:
I do believe I found an answer. I was reading through the discussion threads on the Mplus website and noticed someone else asked the same question. The response they received was that the models are indeed nested:

"Yes, the chi-square difference testing is fine and H0 is nested within H1. This is so even though H0 has Delta and factor mean parameters free that H1 doesn't have. This is because for H0 we can consider Delta*Lambda as a new Lambda in groups 2, 3, ...(so a constrained Lambda relative to group 1) and similarly factor means being free in groups 2, 3, ... is a way to have a different, constrained threshold vector for groups 2, 3, .... So, H0 places non-linear constraints on the H1 model."

http://www.statmodel.com/discussion/messages/23/25.html
